record.paper_title: Open Questions in Stellar Helium Burning Studied with Real Photons
record.original_question: What is the 12C(α, γ)16O reaction cross section at the helium-burning Gamow peak near 300 keV, equivalently the p-wave and d-wave astrophysical S-factors SE1(300) and SE2(300), when they are determined directly enough to reach about 10% accuracy for stellar-helium-burning models? The source identifies this as unresolved because the 16N beta-delayed alpha-emission constraints do not sufficiently determine the p-wave contribution, a low SE1(300) value cannot yet be excluded, and existing lower-energy measurements are not precise enough to settle the issue.

evidence.quote: one must extract the cross section of the 12C(α, γ)16O reaction at the Gamow peak (300 keV) with high accuracy of approximately 10% or better. This goal has not been achieved despite repeated strong statements that appeared in the literature. Constraint from the beta-delayed alpha-particle emission of 16N were shown to not sufficiently restrict the p-wave cross section factor; e.g. a low value of SE1(300) can not be ruled out. Measurements at low energies, are thus mandatory for determining the elusive cross section factor for the 12C(α, γ)16O reaction.

one must extract the p-wave [SE1(300)] and d-wave [SE2(300)] cross section of the 12C(α, γ)16O reaction at the Gamow peak (300 keV) with high accuracy of approximately 10% or better to completely understand stellar helium burning, and better understand Type II and Type Ia supernova.

an independent R-matrix analysis of the world data including the beta decay of 16N data was found to not rule out a small S-factor solution (10-20 keV-b). It is thus doubtful that one can extract the p-wave cross section factor with a reasonable accuracy as stated in Ref. 8. The confusion in this field mandates a direct measurement of the cross section of the 12C(α, γ)16O reaction at low energies.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the radiative alpha-capture reaction $^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\mathrm{O}$, whose cross section near the helium-burning Gamow peak energy $E_{\mathrm{c.m.}} \approx 300$ keV controls the carbon-to-oxygen ratio produced during stellar helium burning. Define the astrophysical S-factor by
$$S(E) = E\,\sigma(E)\,\exp(2\pi\eta(E)),$$
where $\sigma(E)$ is the c.m. cross section and $\eta(E) = Z_\alpha Z_C e^2/(\hbar v)$ is the Sommerfeld parameter. Decompose the ground-state capture cross section into its dominant electric-dipole (p-wave, E1) and electric-quadrupole (d-wave, E2) multipole components, yielding partial S-factors $S_{E1}(E)$ and $S_{E2}(E)$.

Determine the numerical values of $S_{E1}(300\text{ keV})$ and $S_{E2}(300\text{ keV})$ to a total accuracy of approximately $10\%$ or better, using direct experimental input (rather than relying solely on extrapolations from higher-energy capture data and from R-matrix analyses incorporating the $\beta$-delayed $\alpha$-emission spectrum of $^{16}\mathrm{N}$), in such a way that small-$S_{E1}(300)$ solutions (e.g., values in the range $10$–$20$ keV·b) can be definitively excluded or confirmed.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent analyses (including a 2024 multilevel R-matrix study incorporating prospective $^{16}\mathrm{O}(e,e'\alpha)^{12}\mathrm{C}$ data) continue to extrapolate $S_{E1}(300)$ and $S_{E2}(300)$ with uncertainties substantially larger than 10%, and published values from different methods still disagree (e.g., $S_{E1}(300)\sim 80$–$100$ keV·b and $S_{E2}(300)\sim 40$–$70$ keV·b with sizable error bars). No direct sub-Gamow-peak measurement has yet achieved the 10% goal, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: 16O(e,e'α)12C measurements and the 12C(α,γ)16O astrophysical reaction rate
status_evidence.snippet: Multilevel R-matrix analysis used to extrapolate SE1(300 keV) and SE2(300 keV); studies role of new (e,e'α) data in reducing uncertainty.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, SE1(300) and SE2(300) are still being extrapolated via R-matrix analyses with substantial uncertainty.

status_evidence.title: The astrophysical S factor of 12C(α,γ)16O at stellar energy
status_evidence.claim: Reported uncertainties on the partial S-factors at 300 keV remain well above 10%.

status_evidence.title: 12C(20Ne,16O)16O α-transfer reaction and astrophysical S-factors at 300 keV
status_evidence.snippet: Indirect transfer-reaction extraction of S-factors at 300 keV.
status_evidence.claim: Indirect methods continue to be pursued, indicating direct 10%-precision determination has not been achieved.
